Fully Functional Balvatika

How the numbers are computed

Two definitions, scored separately

The SSD tab scores schools on the mentor supportive supervision data using its own five KPIs. The Self-report tab scores schools on the educator's own form using its nine KPIs. Each tab has its own set of ticks and neither affects the other.

What a tick means

Tick the answers that should count as a Yes. Any one ticked answer meets that KPI — options are never required together. A KPI with nothing ticked drops out of that definition rather than failing every school.

The merge

A school is fully functional on the Merged tab if it is fully functional under the SSD definition, or under the self-report definition, or both. Where a school sits in both sources, whichever definition it satisfies is the one that counts. The two are never required to agree.

This is a verdict-level merge, not a KPI-level one. A school does not mix KPIs across sources to build a pass: it must clear a whole definition on one side or the other. That keeps each reported figure traceable to one instrument.

Coverage

6,099 schools in total: 2,677 have both instruments, 1,631 only the self-report, 1,791 only a mentor visit. A school with only one source can only ever be judged by that source's definition.

Which schools are counted

One row per school, keyed on UDISE. Mentor codes arrive without their leading zero and are padded to 11 digits before matching. Self-report rows keep the most recent response per school, and only educators teaching 3-6 or 5-6 year olds.

Reading the figures

A count only means something alongside the definition that produced it. The line under the headline always names the KPIs being counted; the sidebar always shows which answers are ticked.
